Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

get worse verb

also worsen, turn out for the worse, go downhill, become worse

classical

Cic. Div. 2.6.16: ingravēscēns morbus (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 10.4.2: alter in diēs ingravēscit (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 112, 409

ingravēscō, ingravēscere

verb, third conjugation, inchoative, intransitive

get worse, grow more serious (of an illness, a trouble)

Literally “to grow heavy”: an illness or a trouble becomes heavier. “Day by day” is in diēs.

Other words

  • in pejōrem partem vertī — turn out for the worse

    vertor, vertī, versus sum, passive of vertō · also used · modern · Traupman 112, 409

    Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase. Lewis & Short has in pejus and in dēterius, for the worse (Cels. 2.2; Tac. A. 14.43).

  • in dēterius — for the worse

    also used · classical · Tac. A. 14.43 (Lewis & Short s.v. in); Tac. A. 2.82: cūncta aucta in dēterius (Lewis & Short s.v. dēterior)

See also bad.
